Trump says terror plot suspects 'looking to do big damage' after arrests near RAF base used by US

US president Donald Trump has said a suspected terror plot against an RAF base used by the US Air Force (USAF) was "looking to do big damage".

Five men were arrested on Sunday on suspicion of explosive and terrorism offences after armed police stopped three vans in the early hours of the morning.

Mr Trump hailed the UK police response, while suggesting authorities already had the suspects under investigation.

"We had them under investigation. They, they were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great."

Three "suspicious vehicles" travelling towards RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire were reported to police at approximately 12.45am on Sunday.

The men were subsequently arrested by armed officers in the Whelford area under suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were then further arrested under suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act.

About 85 households have been evacuated from their homes near RAF Fairford, which is used by the United States Air Force (USAF).

A major incident was declared by police and a large emergency services presence was seen in the area, including a Hazardous Area Response Team within a 400-metre cordon.
